title: Classic White Sandwich Bread

items.raw: 3½ cups (455 g) all-purpose or bread flour
1 cup (240 g) whole milk, warmed to about 105°F
3 tablespoons (42 g) unsalted butter, softened, plus more for the pan

steps.text: Combine the flour, yeast, sugar, and salt in a large bowl or stand mixer. Add the warm milk, water, and soft butter and mix until a shaggy dough forms.

Knead 8 to 10 minutes by hand or 6 to 7 minutes with a dough hook on medium-low, until smooth, elastic, and slightly tacky. A small piece should stretch thin enough to see light through without tearing.
Shape into a ball, place in a lightly greased bowl, cover, and let rise in a warm spot 1 to 1½ hours, until doubled.
Butter a 9×5-inch loaf pan. Press the dough into a rectangle about 9 inches wide, then roll it up tightly from a short side, pinching the seam closed. Set it in the pan seam side down.
Cover and let rise 45 to 60 minutes, until the top crowns about 1 inch above the rim. Heat the oven to 350°F while it rises.
Bake 35 to 40 minutes, until golden brown and the center reads 190°F on an instant-read thermometer. Tent with foil after 20 minutes if it is browning too quickly.
Turn out onto a rack immediately. Brush the top with melted butter for a soft crust. Cool completely before slicing.

notes.label: Active dry yeast
notes.text: use the same amount, but dissolve it in the warm milk and water for 5 minutes before adding the dry ingredients.

notes.label: Too hot kills yeast
notes.text: milk above about 120°F will slow or kill the yeast. Warm to the touch is right.

notes.label: Storage
notes.text: keeps 3 days wrapped at room temperature; slice before freezing so you can toast from frozen.

notes.label: Variations
notes.text: swap 1 cup of the flour for whole wheat, or use honey in place of the sugar.
